title: U.S. House · Arizona's 8th District
area: Northwest Phoenix metro area in Maricopa County, including Peoria, Surprise, Sun City, Sun City West, Anthem and part of Glendale.

candidates.name: Abraham Hamadeh

summary.text: Abraham "Abe" Hamadeh is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 8th Congressional District, elected in 2024. A former Maricopa County prosecutor and U.S. Army Reserve intelligence officer, he lost the 2022 race for Arizona Attorney General by 280 votes after a recount. He serves on the Armed Services and Veterans' Affairs committees.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1991; his official bio says he was raised in Arizona's 8th District and is the son of immigrants who fled oppressive regimes in the Middle East.
Earned an undergraduate degree in political science from Arizona State University in 2012 and a J.D. from the University of Arizona College of Law in 2016.

Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 2016 to 2022, reaching the rank of Captain and serving as an intelligence officer, including a 14-month deployment to Saudi Arabia negotiating military sales and training the country's domestic security forces.
Worked as a prosecutor in the Maricopa County Attorney's Office, beginning shortly after passing the Arizona bar in 2016 and resigning in September 2021, according to Wikipedia.
Ran for Arizona Attorney General in 2022, winning the Republican primary and losing to Democrat Kris Mayes by 280 votes after an automatic recount; his court challenges to the result were rejected.

Announced his run for Arizona's 8th District in October 2023 after Rep. Debbie Lesko announced her retirement, won a crowded Republican primary, and defeated Democrat Greg Whitten in the November 5, 2024 general election with 56.5% of the vote, per Wikipedia.

Took office January 3, 2025; serves on the House Armed Services Committee (Intelligence and Special Operations, Tactical Air and Land Forces, and Strategic Forces subcommittees) and the Veterans' Affairs Committee (Economic Opportunity and Health subcommittees).
Advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 69,182 votes.

positions.summary: Announced delivering $7 million in federal funding to support Arizona law enforcement.
Urged the Senate to pass the SAVE America Act, which his office's release describes as requiring voters to present valid ID in federal elections and verifying proof of citizenship.
positions.quote: I am proud to support the SAVE America Act.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2025-2026), on the Economic Opportunity and Health subcommittees.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (2025-2026), on the Intelligence and Special Operations, Strategic Forces, and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.

candidates.researchNotes: Hamadeh has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this 2026 race; his 2022 survey answers were for the Attorney General race and are not used here for issue positions. No detailed 2026 issues page or platform statement was found within the research window beyond his committee record.

summary.text: Bernadette Greene Placentia is the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 8th Congressional District. Born in Galesburg, Illinois, she describes herself as a former long-haul truck driver and small-fleet owner who later managed campaigns for other candidates. She won the July 2026 Democratic primary and says she is running as a non-professional politician.

background.text: Born in Galesburg, Illinois; attended the University of Arizona.

Describes a trucking career of over 27 years and 3.5 million miles as a long-haul driver and small fleet/small business owner; she says that career ended because of economic conditions she attributes to "Bidenomics."
Afterward worked as a campaign manager for multiple candidates, according to her Candidate Connection survey.
Describes herself as a pro-choice, pro-union, life-long gun owner and "Conservative Democrat" who is not a professional politician.
Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary for Arizona's 8th District, defeating Raymond Keeler 65.7% to 34.3%.

priorities.text: Says she would fight to protect Social Security, expand Medicare and Medicaid, and support public schools and veterans.
Says she supports securing the border while recognizing the need for legal workers, and wants to increase pay, training and mental-health resources for law enforcement.
Describes herself as a pro-choice, pro-union, lifelong gun owner and self-described 'Conservative Democrat' who supports strengthening borders while protecting rights.

positions.summary: Says she would work to expand Medicare and Medicaid and protect Social Security.
positions.quote: I will fight to protect Social Security, expand Medicare and Medicaid, support our public schools, our Veterans and I want to increase support for Law Enforcement via better pay, better training, better equipment and better access to mental health care

positions.summary: Describes herself as pro-choice and says she would defend women's healthcare rights.
positions.quote: I’m a pro-choice, pro-union, pro-Ukraine, life-long gun owner & Conservative Democrat.

positions.summary: Says tax breaks for billionaires need to end while paying down the debt without cutting essential social services.
positions.quote: the tax breaks for billionaires needs to end
